LESSON: PRODUCTION

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: BUSINESS STUDIES
Strand: Business and Its Environment
Topic 2.5: production
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers production, part of Business and Its Environment in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 BUSINESS STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: Why is production important in an economy? 2. How do we determine the types of costs in a production unit?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on production together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: learner organizes own learning when searching for types of costs in a production unit.

● Self-efficacy: learner develops effective communication skills when debating on the advantages and disadvantages

of division of labour and specialization.

● Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: learner develops skills of interpretation and inference when computing

types of costs in production.

● Creativity and imagination: learner develops inquisitive skills when designing a product label in print or tactile

format.

28

Values:
● Love: learner respects others when brainstorming and presenting on the meaning and importance of production.

● Peace: learner displays tolerance when discussing factors of production required to produce goods and service.

● Respect: learner shows open-mindedness when discussing factors of production required to produce goods and

service.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Mental Health: learner develops emotional awareness to relate well with peers when brainstorming and presenting

on the meaning and importance of production.

● Peer Education and Mentorship: the learner develops interpersonal relationships when discussing and presenting

on the factors of production.

● Financial literacy: learner enhances financial skills when computing production costs.

● Social cohesion: learner cooperates and participates when role playing the functions and responsibilities of a

producer to the consumer.
